Short position closed when XD-RangeSwitch buffer 1 (UpTrend) is non-zero and not EMPTY_VALUE (opposite trend detected, not signal)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MMMode=LOT means fixed lot sizing; other MarginMode values may switch to deposit fraction method. The MM input (0.1) is interpreted as lot size when MMMode=LOT, or as deposit fraction otherwise.

custom_logic_notes: The 'Direct' input (Mode enum) inverts the buffer mapping: TrueDirect maps buffers 1/3 to Up and 0/2 to Dn; FalshDirect (default) swaps them so buffers 0/2 become Up and 1/3 become Dn. This effectively reverses the trading signal direction. Signal gating uses BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose boolean inputs to independently control entry and exit permissions. The XD-RangeSwitch indicator has 4 buffers: buffer 0 and 1 are trend buffers, buffer 2 and 3 are signal buffers. The Recount mechanism forces recalculation on data errors. Signal timestamps (UpSignalTime, DnSignalTime) are derived from SERIES_LASTBAR_DATE + TimeShiftSec.
python_conversion_notes: The XD-RangeSwitch custom indicator logic must be reverse-engineered or reimplemented in Python since it's loaded via iCustom. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh library provides BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, GlobalVariableDel_, and LoadHistory functions that handle order execution, position management, and global variable cleanup - all need Python equivalents. The Direct mode flag swaps which indicator buffers map to Up vs Dn signals, which is a simple buffer remapping in Python. The new bar detection uses CIsNewBar class from the included library. SL/TP values are in points (1000/2000) which need proper point-to-price conversion accounting for broker digit conventions.
